# #2051: Patch: the replays list reads a page in a few queries instead of ninety
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The replays screen is one of the client's hot reads. Building one page of ten rows currently costs the database close to ninety statements — the row list, then several more queries per row to learn each match's mode and result — all inside one transaction. After this patch the same page is built in a small constant number of queries, so the screen loads faster and holds a database connection for a fraction of the time.

## Why

`api/replays.rs:444-449` calls `replays_list` (page + 1), then `matches_mode_of` once per replay. Each `matches_mode_of` (`db/pg.rs:3488-3525`) runs a GIN-indexed `series_with_game` probe plus a mode select; inside `replays_list`, `replay_row` (`db/pg.rs:3640-3661`) adds a `matches` select and `results_get_by_match` per row. With a `run_as` statement per store call (`db/pg.rs:512-520`), a `REPLAY_LIST_PAGE = 10` page is roughly 1 + 2×11 + 2×10 + 1 = 44 logical calls — ~88 sequential statements over the pooler. The in-memory fake answers instantly, so only Postgres shows the cost.

## Proposal

A batched `replays_list` variant that joins `matches`, `results` and the action count and derives each row's mode in one query (the series/room/ticket precedence mirrors `matches_mode_of`), keeping the already-batched `profiles_get_many` opponent read. Fake and Postgres change symmetrically; the existing `contract.rs` `replays` module already asserts row equality between them.

## Where it lands

`crates/server/src/api/replays.rs`, `crates/server/src/db/pg.rs`, `crates/server/src/db/fake.rs`, `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A page costs a constant small number of statements regardless of page size
- [ ] Fake and Postgres return identical rows (the contract tests prove it)
- [ ] No change to the response shape or pagination behaviour

## Size and risks

Medium: mostly SQL join work. The contract suite gives parity coverage for free; the risk is a subtly wrong mode derivation, which the same suite's row-equality assertions cover.

| `crates/server/src/db/fake.rs` | change | New `pub fn replays_list_with_modes`: one `call(f, "replays.listWithModes")`, reusing `replay_row_in` and `match_mode_in` |

| `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs` | change | New parity test in `mod replays`, registered in its `both_stores!` |

No new ruling: this is a pure performance refactor with identical observable behaviour, so no spec decision is being made.

## Steps

1. `crates/server/src/db/store.rs`: add `ReplayWithMode` directly after `ReplayRow` (line 699), deriving the same traits (`Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Debug, PartialEq`), with fields `replay: ReplayRow` and `mode: Option<QueueMode>`. Add `Tx::replays_list_with_modes` directly after `replays_get` (line 2107) via the existing `dispatch!` macro, with a doc comment stating the contract: the same rows, order, limit and offset semantics as `replays_list`, each paired with what `matches_mode_of` answers for that match.
2. `crates/server/src/db/pg.rs`: add `pub async fn replays_list_with_modes` after `replays_list` (line 3697). Keep `replays_list`, `replay_row`, `matches_mode_of`, `series_with_game` and `results_get_by_match` untouched. Behaviour, in order: return empty when `!is_uuid(profile_id)`, exactly as `replays_list` does; one `run_as(t, None).await?`; one `SELECT` joining `public.matches m` to `public.results r` on `r.match_id = m.id`, with the existing `WHERE` (status over, seat held, result exists, log exists) and `ORDER BY m.ended_at desc nulls last, m.id desc` plus limit/offset. Select the match columns enumerated with `m.` prefixes (same list as `match_columns!`, so `MatchDbRow::read` still reads them by bare name), the result columns aliased (`r.match_id AS r_match_id`, and likewise for every column `ResultDbRow::read` needs), `(select count(*) from public.match_actions a where a.match_id = m.id) AS actions`, `m.mode AS own_mode, m.room_code, m.room_mode`, the ticket subselect copied from `matches_mode_of` (`select t.mode ... order by t.enqueued_at, t.id limit 1) AS ticket_mode`), and `exists (select 1 from public.series s where s.state -> 'games' @> jsonb_build_array(jsonb_build_object('matchId', m.id::text))) AS in_series` (the same containment `series_with_game` probes, evaluated per row). Per returned row: `MatchDbRow::read` then `to_match`, emptying a deleted second seat exactly as `replay_row` does (`row.p2_profile_id.get_or_insert_with(String::new)`); build the `ResultRow` from the `r_`-aliased columns via `to_result`; derive `mode` with the precedence copied from `matches_mode_of` lines 3492–3524 (in series → `bo3`; own mode → it; room code set → `room_mode` or `bo1`; else ticket mode), using `queue_mode_of`/`from_literal`.
3. `crates/server/src/db/fake.rs`: add `pub fn replays_list_with_modes` after `replays_list` (line 1751). One `call(f, "replays.listWithModes")?`, then the same filter/sort/paginate body as `replays_list` (finished, seat held, `replay_row_in`, `actions > 0`; newest `finished_at` first, id breaking ties; skip/take), mapping each row to `ReplayWithMode { replay, mode: match_mode_in(tables, &row.id) }`. No other fake function changes.
4. `crates/server/src/api/replays.rs` (`list_replays`, lines 442–459): replace `tx.replays_list` plus the `modes` loop with one `tx.replays_list_with_modes(&profile.id, page + 1, offset).await?` call; keep the `more`/truncate logic, the `profiles_get_many` opponent read and the commit exactly as they are; build each `ReplayListing` from `entry.replay` and `entry.mode`. Update the comment above the call to name the single batched read.
5. `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs` (`mod replays`, after line 6371): add `async fn replays_list_with_modes_matches_the_per_row_reads`, reusing the mod's `a_match` helper for plain rows and copying the fixture shapes from the R376 test for one room match (rooms_create, rooms_claim, matches_create), one queue match (tickets_insert × 2, tickets_claim_pair, matches_create), one series game (series_create with a `games` entry, matches_create), one rematch (match_row with `mode` spread), one sourceless match, and one deleted-opponent replay. Finish each with a result and a log. Assert the new method's output equals `replays_list` zipped with per-row `matches_mode_of` for several limit/offset pairs, and that sourceless, resultless, logless and live rows stay excluded. Register it in the `both_stores!` at line 6479.
6. `crates/server/tests/api/replays.rs` (`mod r768_the_list`): add `r768_the_list_reads_a_page_in_a_constant_number_of_store_calls`. Seed two finished matches, install an `on_call` hook that pushes each called name into an `Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Vec<String>>>` and returns `Ok(())` (copy the hook assignment from the `r768_the_list_folds_nothing…` test), `GET /api/replays`, record the sorted call list; seed three more finished matches, `GET` again, and assert the identical list: exactly one `replays.listWithModes`, one `profiles.getMany`, and no `matches.modeOf`, `replays.list` or per-row result reads.
7. Run the checks in Tests, then `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

## Tests

- Contract parity (both stores; Postgres half runs under `DATABASE_URL` via `sh crates/server/tests/db/run.sh`): `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server_store store::contract::replays` — includes the new `replays_list_with_modes_matches_the_per_row_reads` in `memory` always and `postgres` when the database is set. It fails without the fix because the new method does not exist; a wrong mode precedence fails the room/ticket/series/own-mode assertions.
- API cost (fake store): `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server api::replays::r768_the_list` — includes the new constant-calls test, which fails on the old code (one `matches.modeOf` per row) and passes when the page costs one list call plus one profiles call however many rows it holds.
- Existing coverage kept green: the untouched `r768_lists_finished_matches_with_a_kept_log_newest_first` contract test and the `r768_the_list` API tests prove no change to rows, ordering, pagination or response shape.
- Lint and format: `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`. No `spec check` impact: no ruling note is added or cited.

## Done when

- [ ] One page costs one list read plus the existing batched opponent read, regardless of page size (the API test proves the call count is constant).
- [ ] Fake and Postgres return identical rows and modes for every mode source — series game, own rematch mode, room, queue ticket, none — plus pagination, deleted opponents and excluded rows (the contract test proves it on both stores).
- [ ] Response shape and pagination behaviour are unchanged (existing list tests still pass unmodified).
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server_store store::contract::replays`, `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server api::replays::r768_the_list`, `cargo fmt --check` and the clippy command above all pass.

## Risks

- A subtly wrong mode precedence in the new Postgres query (e.g. checking the row's own mode before the series probe, or misreading a null `room_mode` as sourceless instead of `bo1`) would mislabel rows on the replays screen. Avoided by applying the precedence in Rust with the same order and helpers as `matches_mode_of`, and by the contract test covering all five sources on both stores.
- Column-name collisions in the joined `SELECT` (both tables carry `match_id` and seat ids) would silently misread rows. Avoided by aliasing every result column with an `r_` prefix and leaving match columns under their natural names for the existing row readers.
- Statement-count regressions hiding in `run_as`: each store method issues one, so the new path is exactly two `run_as` plus two data statements per page (list, opponents). Avoided by keeping the method count at two and asserting it in the API test.

## Open questions

None. Every choice above is pinned; the one alternative considered — deriving the mode in SQL `CASE` instead of Rust — was rejected because it duplicates the precedence in a second language where the contract suite cannot read it as directly.
